ai_practice: Senior engineers use agentic coding tools (Claude Code) every day; new TypeScript, React, Node and Postgres codebase with an agent instructions file and test commands from day one.

items.move_up: Writing down the distributor's current order, approval and QuickBooks routines before the workshops would turn more of this into drafting.
Read-only API access to a copy of the real QuickBooks company file before kickoff would turn most of the audit into scripted queries.
Agreeing field ownership per synced entity before the design session would make the model checkable against written rules.
Starting from an existing B2B portal pattern library and the written acceptance criteria would let AI draft more of the flows.
Adopting an off-the-shelf design system and theming it, instead of designing one, would move this up.
Using the auth provider's hosted sign-in pages would leave less security code for the agent to write.
A written invite-token spec (expiry, single use, rate limits) would let the agent work against tests instead of review.
A permission matrix written as test fixtures before coding would make every authorization change machine-checked.
Settling the approval edge cases (limit changes, approver absent, multiple approvers) in writing before the build would move this up.
Reusing the authorization layer from E13 unchanged keeps this to screens and tests.
Knowing where customer prices live (the first open question) would remove the main ambiguity.
A Stripe test-mode account with webhook fixtures and recorded multi-invoice scenarios from day one would move this up the band.
Replaying recorded Stripe event sequences (out-of-order, duplicate, failed) in CI would make the webhook handler fully machine-checked.
Starting the Intuit production-key review in week one and keeping token handling in a small, tested module would move this up.
A recorded QuickBooks sandbox harness that simulates throttling and missed webhooks would give the agent a pass/fail check.
A cleaned export of the real customer list with the distributor's matching rules written down would move this up.
Confirming where prices and stock live would turn this into a mapping exercise against a known API.
A sandbox company configured with the distributor's real tax and terms setup would let tests check invoice output end to end.
Recorded change-data-capture payloads for edits, voids and credit memos would make this testable offline.
An hour with the distributor's bookkeeper to write down the deposit and fee entries would remove the tacit-knowledge block.
Written field-ownership rules per entity would shrink the conflict cases and make each one a test.
Agreed mismatch tolerances written as test cases would make the report checkable.
A copy of the production company file for repeated dry runs, with validation counts as checks, would move this up.
Reusing the customer authorization layer for staff roles instead of a second one would cut the security-sensitive code.
Stable sandbox fixtures and recorded third-party responses would cut the flaky-test triage.
Scanner and authorization-test gates in CI from week one would leave fewer findings for the final review.
Turning each piece of UAT feedback into a failing test before fixing it would move the rework up the band.
A rehearsed cutover on staging with the same scripts and checklists would make most steps repeatable and checkable.
Keeping decision records and runbooks current during the build leaves only the walkthrough for the end.
Production logs and alerts wired to reproducible test cases would turn more incidents into reproducible bugs.
